## 2

I understand why you might be skeptical, especially since we rely on images and information provided by institutions. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend only on NASA photographs. Ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, different stars are visible from different parts of Earth, lunar eclipses show Earth casting a round shadow, and people can circumnavigate the globe. Independent space agencies, companies, astronomers, and ordinary observers around the world also track satellites and communicate with them. Faking all of that consistently would be far more complicated than accepting what the evidence shows: Earth is approximately spherical.

## 3

Sunlight may look white, but it is actually made of many colors, like the colors in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of air. Blue light gets scattered in many directions more easily than most of the other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more air, scattering away much of the blue and leaving more red, orange, and pink light to reach us.
